title: Move-Out Damage Assessment from Photos

blueprintSignals.name: Change detection
blueprintSignals.definition: pixel-level difference between aligned move-in and move-out photos after exposure normalisation
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Lighting changes look like damage, so normalise first

blueprintSignals.name: Damage class
blueprintSignals.definition: classifier probability for stain, hole, scratch, crack or burn
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Rare classes have few examples, so check per class

blueprintSignals.name: Age of fixture
blueprintSignals.definition: years since the fixture, flooring or paint was installed or last renewed
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Records are incomplete, so use building age as a fallback

blueprintSignals.name: Repair cost table
blueprintSignals.definition: local labour and material rates per repair type
blueprintSignals.asOfRule: Rates vary by contractor and season, so use a range

engineFeatures.meaning: how strongly a region stands out from its neighbourhood
the strongest local contrast anywhere in the image
contrast divided by the image's own noise level
which scanner or camera produced the image
augmentation that stops the model using overall brightness

label: For "Move-Out Damage Assessment from Photos": Compare move-in and move-out photos to identify damage beyond normal wear and estimate repair cost for deposit decisions. Define the label exactly as in milestone M1: what counts as a positive or a correct outcome, and when it becomes known. Design around this trap first: Posed photos taken by a careful inspector are cleaner than tenants' own pictures.
